definitions.explanation: A casual short-sleeved shirt with a collar and a few buttons at the neck, typically made of knitted cotton.

examples.japanese: ⟦{白|しろ}い→白い：00587_shiroi⟧ポロシャツ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}ている→着る：00541_kiru⟧。
examples.english: I'm wearing a white polo shirt.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ポロシャツ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{涼|すず}しくて→涼しい：00674_suzushii⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: Polo shirts are nice and cool in summer.

examples.japanese: ⟦クールビズ→クールビズ：29551_kuurubizu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時期|じき}→時期：03269_jiki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、ポロシャツ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{出勤|しゅっきん}→出勤：04548_shukkin⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: During the Cool Biz period, many people come to work in polo shirts.

notes:
A Japanese coinage from English "polo" and "shirt" (⟦シャツ→シャツ：01052_shatsu⟧). In Japan, polo shirts occupy a middle ground between formal and casual — too relaxed for formal business but acceptable in many semi-casual workplace settings, especially during summer.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ポロシャツ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}る→着る：00541_kiru⟧: to wear a polo shirt
- ⟦{半袖|はんそで}→半袖：15518_hansode⟧ポロシャツ: short-sleeved polo shirt
- ⟦{長袖|ながそで}→長袖：15517_nagasode⟧ポロシャツ: long-sleeved polo shirt
- ポロシャツ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧チノパン: polo shirt with chinos (typical casual style)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Since Japan's Cool Biz campaign (encouraging lighter clothing in summer to reduce air conditioning), polo shirts have become more accepted in offices. Some companies include them in their dress code as appropriate summer attire.

RELATED CLOTHING TERMS:
- Tシャツ: T-shirt — more casual, no collar
- ⟦ワイシャツ→ワイシャツ：01068_waishatsu⟧: dress shirt — more formal, typically with a full button front
- ⟦カットソー→カットソー：28534_kattosoo⟧: cut-and-sewn top — a broader category of knitted casual tops
